extracted.intended_audience: philosophers and creative writers interested in Bergson's theory of life and creativity
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts philosophical criteria about creation, intuition, repetition, and order from Bergson's Creative Evolution that can inform creative practice (e.g., originality, sustaining intuition, relation of form and matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generality based on likeness (generalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is _likeness_ between individuals of the same species and between complex physical effects obtained by the same composition of causes, and this likeness makes generalization possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical interest lies in this common character: our daily life expects the same things and situations, so we designate laws (inert matter) and genera (life) similarly for practice. Use likeness as the basis for generalization, but beware conflating the different origins of likeness in life and in physical systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish 'vital' (willed) order from physical (automatic) order
rubrics_metrics.description: The vital order secures constancy of effect even when causes vary (analogous to a 'willed' order), whereas the physical order makes the same composition of causes give the same combined effect ('automatic').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate the two kinds of order: when assessing or producing work, recognize whether similarity/repetition arises from an internal creative impulse (vital) or from repeated mechanical causes (physical). This distinction matters for interpretation and for valuing originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid equating laws (relations) with genera (individuals)
rubrics_metrics.description: The generality of mathematical laws (relations between terms) is essentially a comparison performed by intelligence; genera are tied to individual objects and heredity and have a different ontological status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In theorizing or critiquing creative work, avoid reducing living, individuated phenomena to mere relations or universal laws; recognize when an account improperly explains genera by laws or vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition in life is accidental, in physics essential
rubrics_metrics.description: Successive impressions in printing are identical, whereas representatives of one species are never entirely the same; heredity transmits both characters and the impetus for change (vitality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value subtle difference within repetition: in creative practice, exact repetition is mechanical, while recurrent motifs in living creativity should carry variation and impetus for novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chance and disorder are relative to expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: When one expects one of the two orders (willed or automatic) and finds the other, one calls the result 'chance' or 'disorder'; these ideas objectify a state of mind rather than absolute negations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret apparent randomness in work as a function of perspective and expectations; what seems 'disordered' may reflect use of a different order or intention. Avoid treating chance as absolute rather than relative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consciousness as the principle that detends (releases tension) to extend (create)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consciousness must detach from the already-made and attach to the being-made; it is a retrospective vision that makes will and seeing one, enabling creation (though this effort is hard to sustain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative practice requires temporarily aligning perception with volition—turning back on oneself to grasp the becoming rather than the done. Exercises that reorient attention from product to process help sustain creative acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustain and reinstate intuition against dialectic
rubrics_metrics.description: Intuition vivifies systems and gives access to truth; dialectic (conceptual analysis) is necessary to communicate and test intuition but tends to dissipate it. The philosopher/artist must repeatedly return to intuition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In creation and critique: use analytic tools to refine and transmit ideas, but continually re-enter intuitive experience to keep originality and direct contact with the creative principle. Beware over-intellectualizing to the point of losing creative insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation is formation, not addition of atomic elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet creates a poem though no new letters are invented; creation brings new form from pre-existing elements rather than new atomic constituents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess originality by new organization and emergent form rather than by invention of wholly new basic units. In producing work, focus on novel arrangements and the emergent qualities they produce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation by interruption — fixation of form through arrest
rubrics_metrics.description: A creation of matter (or a fixed work) can result from an interruption of the creative current: when action that generates form pauses, it can congeal into durable matter or form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the role of stopping, editing, and freezing a process to produce a finished form; deliberate interruption can be a creative device that yields a stable work from ongoing activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life counteracts material degradation by retarding it
rubrics_metrics.description: Life behaves as if working in the inverse direction of material mutability: it cannot stop physical degradation but succeeds in retarding it, continuing an initial impulsion to richer activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value creative acts as forces that resist entropy of sameness; in critique and practice, emphasize works that introduce or preserve complexity and variation against homogenizing tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer growth and continuous creation over a one-stroke total genesis
rubrics_metrics.description: The universe (and creative reality) is not a totality made once for all but is being made continually; the habit of conceiving a single creation or eternal matter obscures concrete time and growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame narratives and creative processes as ongoing, developmental, and temporal rather than as static, finalized origins. Embrace process, emergence, and cumulative change as central to meaningful creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish quantitative conventions from metaphysical direction (conservation vs degradation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The conservation of energy is in part conventional (measurement-dependent), whereas the degradation of energy (entropy) points to a metaphysical direction independent of measurement: changes tend toward uniform, invisible states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using scientific metaphors in creative work or theory, be mindful of what is measurement-conventional versus what conveys qualitative, directional meaning (e.g., decline of variety). Use entropy metaphorically to describe loss of heterogeneity and the need for creative renewal.
